'''Aleksandr Ivanovich Nekrasov''' ({{langx|ru|Алекса́ндр Ива́нович Некра́сов}}; {{Gregorian to Julian|9 December 1883}} – 21 May 1957) was a Soviet and Russian [[mathematician]] known for his mathematical contributions to [[Fluid mechanics|hydromechanics]] and [[aeromechanics]]. The [[Nekrasov integral equation]] describing surface waves is named for him.<ref>{{cite journal |last=Kuznetsov |first=Nikolay |date=November 2015 |title=333 Pages That Changed Theory of Water Waves |url=https://www.ams.org/notices/201510/rnoti-p1208.pdf |journal=[[Notices of the American Mathematical Society]] |publisher=American Mathematical Society |volume=62 |issue=10 |pages=1208–1209 |doi=10.1090/noti1285 |access-date=13 November 2015|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Biography ==
Nekrasov was born in [[Moscow]], [[Russian Empire]] where he would remain for the rest of his life. He went to school and graduated from the [[Moscow State University|University of Moscow]] in 1906. Nekrasov graduated with a first class diploma.

Nekrasov earned a gold medal for work of his essay, ''Theory of the Satellites of Jupiter''.
